transcript: Yes! I've been saying this for years, and I will take every opportunity I have to talk about it, even if, like in this case, I actually haven't heard Reeve Carney sing The Great Gatsby score. I actually haven't even heard the Great Gatsby score, believe it or not. So I can't speak to whether it suits his voice well or not, but the broader point that this creator is making is one that I feel very strongly about. The Broadway fandom is really unkind to actors who have very idiosyncratic, unusual voices, especially if they are in revivals or replacing roles. This is frustrating on multiple levels, not least of which is that many of the Broadway legends that are so beloved now would probably have been mocked on Theatre TikTok and theatre Reddit if they broke out today. From Carol Channing, Bernadette Peters even to more recently like Michael Cerveris or Idina Menzel. And what we've ended up with in musical theatre is no shortage of incredibly proficient singers, but not enough really compelling actors. Now is Reeve Carney specifically a really exciting actor? I don't know, but any discouragement of vocal diversity in musical theatre is bad for the development of new, exciting talent. I think about someone like Katrina Lenk, who everyone Loved in bands visit, but then as soon as she played Bobbi in company, suddenly she's too weird. Her vocal style is wrong, even though, in my opinion, I think she was delivering a really compelling and skillful performance on an acting level. And I'll say what everyone's too afraid to say. Colton Ryan in New York, New York. Excellent performance. Yes! He was doing something very specific with his voice that was hearkening back to, like, an old school crooner style. He did it well. He was very charismatic and dynamic, but all anyone could say was he sounds like Kermit the frog. Which, by the way, has become the most overused insult for any male performer, especially with any sort of nasal tone to their voice. And people keep saying it like they're eating. Come up with a new insult. Or just get used to voices that don't sound like Aaron Tveit, especially when they're doing something really exciting on an acting level.
